source.title: X-SAM: Boosting Sharpness-Aware Minimization with Dominant-Eigenvector Gradient Correction
source.authors: Hongru Duan; Yongle Chen; Lei Guan

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies SAM variants, gradient directions, and Hessian curvature. It does not test any listed claim version about training classification error, local minima, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-loss trajectories for X-SAM, but not training classification error. Accuracy results are test accuracy. Hessian eigenvalues and gradient-eigenvector angles do not measure the behaviors named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates X-SAM's generalization and curvature control, without testing any listed version. Its discussion of the stability threshold cites prior work; its own experiments do not compare learning rates with that threshold or establish recovery above it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors argue that X-SAM's eigenvector-based gradient correction controls dominant curvature and improves generalization, while acknowledging non-negligible eigenvector-estimation cost. Their claims concern SAM optimization and generalization rather than the listed claim versions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates X-SAM, a SAM variant that intermittently estimates the dominant Hessian eigenvector and attenuates the gradient component along it.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to correction strength α on CIFAR-100 with ResNet-18; α = 0.2 gives the highest test accuracy among tested settings, while accuracy is relatively stable for α in [0.1, 0.4]. This does not test a listed claim version.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.2 describes rapid initial training-loss reduction followed by a slight increase, but the cited plots identify the quantity as test loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: X-SAM exhibits an initially falling loss trajectory under the reported recipes; whether the cited plots show training or test loss requires clarification.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report smaller dominant Hessian eigenvalues under X-SAM and improved or comparable test accuracy against SAM variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dominant-eigenvector gradient correction can reduce measured curvature and improve test accuracy relative to the tested SAM variants.

record.problems: The supplied text gives no numerical training-loss values, and the relevant trajectories appear only in figures. The study reports test accuracy rather than training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results directly measure the claim versions. Test accuracies, Hessian spectra, and gradient-eigenvector angles do not measure the listed training-error claims.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error under SGD or Adam, including model-size, label-corruption, stopping and regularization conditions.
Spurious local-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of activation-matched, Gaussian, orthogonal or convolutional initializations on training speed and trainable depth.
Loss recovery, divergence and sustained loss reduction relative to learning-rate stability thresholds. Curvature reduction under X-SAM alone does not test these behaviors.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply. The loss-label inconsistency prevents treating R1 and R2 as verified training-loss measurements. Even verified training loss would not establish V1's training classification error or V5's threshold-relative dynamics.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error and the effects of model size, random or corrupted labels, and training duration.
Training-error effects of depth, residual shortcuts, special initialization, and normalization.
Training speed and trainable depth under alternative initializations.
Training-loss recovery or divergence across learning rates relative to stability limits.
Training-speed and learning-rate tolerance effects of batch normalization or Fixup.
